column1: # Secret patterns masked in hook and CLI logs — the one source for both
# claude-code/hooks/lib/aa-ma-log.sh (bash) and aa_ma.logsetup (Python).
# Format: <rule id><TAB><regex>. Lines starting with # and blank lines are skipped; any
# other line without exactly one tab, or with an empty regex, makes both readers fail closed.
# Rule ids are the report gate's (src/aa_ma/analysis/secrets.py PATTERNS), so one secret has
# one name across the forge; a test pins the subset. That gate keeps its own regexes: it
# needs lookbehind, named groups and multi-line matching, which bash cannot express.
# Patterns are applied in file order, so a specific rule must precede a broader one that
# would also match it; the generic key=value rules come last, and their value may not start
# with "[" so an already-masked token keeps its specific id. An id may repeat (generic-env
# covers KEY=value and --key value); bearer-token is log-only, the report gate has no such rule.
# Each regex must mean the same thing as POSIX ERE (bash [[ =~ ]]) and Python `re`:
# use bracket classes, [.] for a literal dot, {m,n}; no \d \s \w, lookarounds,
# (?i), lazy quantifiers or backreferences — case-insensitive words are spelt [Pp][Aa]….
# Nothing may match the empty string, and no pattern may match its own replacement
# "[REDACTED:<rule id>]". Masking replaces the whole match, key name included. No unbounded run may precede a fixed
# token (e.g. [a-z]* before "://"): every start position would rescan it, O(n²) on long input.
